title: Physics Module Reliability Contract
description: Well-Architected reliability discipline applied to physics gate modules. Every covered module must publish HOW it fails (failure_mode), WHAT breaks when it does (blast_radius), how it degrades, and how to recover. A green test is not a reliability claim; this contract is.

coverage_floor.description: Ratchet: the number of covered modules must never drop below this. Deleting an entry without lowering the floor (and justifying it) fails the gate.

scope_roots.description: Source roots scanned for INV-bearing physics modules. Uncovered modules under these roots are reported by name as the explicit backlog.

module.description: Path to the physics module, relative to repo root.

invariants.description: Invariants this module is bound to. Each MUST be literally present in the module source (the checker greps for it).

role.description: CLAUDE.md Section 0 gradient role. Protectors have unconditional priority over generators.

layer.description: Maintenance/processing layer. L0 gradient exists, L1 bounded, L2 protected, L3 preserved, L4 utilized.

failure_mode.description: Concrete way the module produces wrong/unphysical output. Should be grounded in the bound invariants' FALSIFICATION clause, not generic.

blast_radius.description: What downstream computation is corrupted if this module fails — named consumers, not 'the system'.

degradation_mode.description: Observable degraded state that precedes hard failure (what to watch).

recovery_command.description: Executable-shaped recovery/rollback or fail-closed action (a runnable command or a named raise path), not prose.

fail_closed.description: True iff the module raises/halts on contract violation rather than emitting a silently repaired value.
